newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease as Yeltsin worries remain.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease as Yeltsin worries remain.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds eased in calm trading on Friday as the market remained overshadowed by concerns over whether President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation would be successful.
Yeltsin said on Thursday he would have a heart operation, probably at the end of September in Moscow.
Prices fell one big figure on Thursday after the news appeared.
A senior Russian surgeon said on Friday Yeltsin would have a bypass operation for ischaemic heart disease at Moscow's Cardiological Centre at the end of September but gave no details.
Dealers said foreign operators had been selling quite actively in early trading, apparently fulfilling client orders. They added that the 2008 maturity was hit most.
"The market is nervous and thin. Nobody is opening new positions because of worries about Yeltsin and the old information that some bonds can be frozen," an International Moscow bank dealer said.
Banking sources told Reuters in late August Russian police were preparing an order to freeze up to a further $7 million nominal of MinFin bonds, which had been stolen.

"What we see today can be called post-panic range-trading. Fluctuations are depending on what this or other client thinks about the (forthcoming heart) operation's result and the market's ability to respond to it," one dealer said.
Dealers said the second, third and fourth tranches were meeting strong support at 75.00, 48.00 and 31.00 respectively. The sixth and seventh tranches are traded much less actively, they said.
They forecast prices were unlikely to fall further next week and expected a stabilisation at current levels.
"Russia looks better compared with some other Eastern Europe instruments, so Western investors are positive rather than negative towards investing here," one dealer said.
"As for Yeltsin, everybody suspected he has some heart problems. The other thing is when it is said clearly," he added.
